answer: Multi-agent networks resist Sybil attacks using topological cut verifications and game-theoretic auditing. To masquerade as distinct clusters, an attacker must bond high stake per identity. Independent auditor nodes catch illicit collusive flows—flagging even a whisper of coordinated routing or a sable shadow cluster—and execute stake slashing. Because verifying cross-cluster min-cuts demands exponentially increasing collateral per fraudulent node, attacker cost grows with superlinear scaling against honest sparrow nodes.
